note.subject: french
note.title: Quick rules
note.overview: This lesson contains 50 enabled questions. It teaches Quick rules through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Quick rules.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Opinion + noun takes le/la/l’/les.
Food and drink quantities take du/de la/de l’/des.
After ne…pas or ne…plus before a noun, use de/d’.
After aller, choose au/à la/à l’/aux from the place noun.
Passé composé = auxiliary + past participle.
Movement/reflexive verbs using être may require agreement.

questionInstructions.label: APPLY THE RULE
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Produce the exact item requested by the rule prompt.

questionInstructions.label: TRANSLATE INTO FRENCH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Translate the quoted English and write the complete French answer.

questionInstructions.label: CORRECT THE ERROR
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Find the error and rewrite the whole corrected sentence.

questionInstructions.label: COMPLETE THE FRENCH
questionInstructions.whatToDo: Do not translate the whole line; write only the word/chunk replacing _____.

workedExamples.prompt: Give the taught example for: Opinions.
workedExamples.answer: J’aime le riz. / Je préfère regarder la télé.
workedExamples.why: With a noun after aimer / adorer / détester / préférer, use the definite article (le / la / l’ / les). With another verb, use the infinitive without an article.

workedExamples.prompt: Give the taught example for: Food & drink.
workedExamples.answer: Je bois de l’eau. / Je mange des frites.
workedExamples.why: When eating or drinking, use du / de la / de l’ / des

workedExamples.prompt: Give the taught example for: Negatives.
workedExamples.answer: Je ne bois pas de coca. / Il n’y a plus de pain.
workedExamples.why: After ne…pas / ne…plus, change to de / d’

workedExamples.prompt: Give the taught example for: Places after aller.
workedExamples.answer: Je vais au cinéma. / à la pharmacie. / à l’épicerie. / aux magasins.
workedExamples.why: Choose au / à la / à l’ / aux carefully

workedExamples.prompt: Give the taught example for: Passé composé.
workedExamples.why: Use auxiliary + past participle

workedExamples.prompt: Give the taught example for: Être verbs.
workedExamples.answer: Elle est allée. / Ils sont sortis.
workedExamples.why: Movement / state verbs often use être and may need agreement

commonMistakes: Keeping du/de la after a negative.

quickCheck.question: Elles ont sorti.

Elles ___ sorties.
Write only the missing word or article.

Correct sentence: Elles sont sorties.
Required grammar job: être verb + agreement
“I like pizza, but I do not eat pizza.”
quickCheck.answer: J’aime la pizza, mais je ne mange pas de pizza.

quickCheck.question: “She went to the pharmacy.”
quickCheck.answer: Elle est allée à la pharmacie.

beforeStartingPractice: Read every must-memorise rule.
Cover the answer column and retrieve at least six chunks.
Complete the 60-second self-check.
On each card, read the task label before the French/English stimulus.
note.markingReminder: Accents are displayed and corrected but not deducted. Base spelling, article, subject, verb form, auxiliary, agreement, negative order and required content are still marked.

note.overview: This lesson contains 138 enabled questions. It teaches Weather, activities and opinions through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Weather, activities and opinions.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Weather chunks use il fait, il y a, il pleut, il neige or il gèle.
Jouer + sport normally uses au/à la/aux; jouer + instrument uses du/de la.
After aimer with a noun, keep the definite article.
A reason needs parce que/car plus a complete idea.
Learn activity verbs as complete je chunks.

note.overview: This lesson contains 123 enabled questions. It teaches Home, family and descriptions through explicit translation, recall, grammar and application tasks.
learningGoals: Recall the core language for Home, family and descriptions.
Identify the task direction before writing.
Explain errors by naming the article, subject, tense, auxiliary, agreement or negative rule.
Use the material in a short controlled sentence.
mustMemoriseRules: Use habiter + place phrase; town names normally take à.
Country prepositions vary: en, au or aux.
Learn family nouns with mon/ma/mes.
Adjectives must agree where their feminine/plural form changes.
Distinguish énervé (feeling annoyed) from énervant (causing annoyance).
